newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SABENA, SWISSAIR AND AUSTRIAN TO BUY AIRBUS PLANES.
newsitem.headline: SABENA, SWISSAIR AND AUSTRIAN TO BUY AIRBUS PLANES.

text.p: Swissair and its partners Austrian Airlines and Sabena have chosen the Airbus A330-200 planes for the renewal of their long-distance fleet, Sabena said on Thursday.
Boeing's B767 plane had been the other main candidate, a Sabena spokesman said. He declined to give financial details.

Sabena said the first A330-200s will be assembled in Toulouse, France, in mid-March and the maiden flight is scheduled for August 1997. The three airlines will receive their first A330-200 in September 1998, it said.
Swissair, which has a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena and 10 percent in Austrian, will replace eight Airbus A310-300s with nine A330-200s.
It said in Zurich that its investment in Airbus jets would total 300 to 400 million Swiss francs.

Austrian said earlier on Thursday it had placed a firm order for four A330-200s worth some four billion schillings ($365.1 million). It said the first plane was expected to be delivered in August 1998 and the second one at the beginning of 1999.
Sabena will immediately order one A330-200 and took an option on up to five more A330-200s, due to be delivered by the year 2000.
Sabena said the decision was approved earlier this week by the boards of directors of the three airlines, which have also linked their frequent flyer programmes.

"The partnership...has allowed a grouped order," the Sabena statement said. "Austrian Airlines, Sabena and Swissair work together within the framework of the purchase and management of these new planes," it said.
Sabena said it would sell its three A310 planes in early 1997 to U.S. plane leasing company ILFC. It will lease three A330-300s until the delivery of the ordered A330-200.
From 1997 its long-distance fleet will consist of four A340, three A330 and two Boeing 747, it said.
It said it wanted to have just two different types of plane in 1998 and only one in 2000, compared with four now. Sabena also has a one McDonnell-Douglas DC-10.

The statement said the criteria which led to the choice of the Airbus A330 were the homogeneity of fleets, the identical configuration with that of the A340 and possibilities regarding synergies between the three partners.
Sabena said that harmonising its fleet would substantially reduce costs as it allowed savings in personnel training and technical support.
"Thanks to this decision...Sabena is hoping to save a few hundreds of millions (of Belgian francs)," it said.
